note: Source of truth for the onboarding battery step (onboarding R7) and for the oem-battery-guide skill. Every entry is sourced from public pages and is UNVERIFIED until a person records a device check in `verified`. Setting names change by phone model and software version; the app shows unverified entries as 'General steps'.

steps.title: Let Outage use the battery
steps: Open Settings, then Battery.
Open Battery Optimization. Tap Outage and choose Don't optimize.
Or open Settings, Battery Lab, Battery Saving Settings. Turn off Power Saving Management For Apps.

steps.title: Let Outage run in the background
steps: Open the Phone Master app, then Toolbox, then Auto-start management.
Turn on Outage.
Open Settings, Apps, Special Access, Background Activity Permissions. Allow Outage.

steps.title: Keep Outage in recent apps
steps: Open the recent apps screen.
On the Outage card, tap the lock icon so it stays open.

steps.title: Turn off power savers that stop apps
steps: In Phone Master, open Power Marathon and turn off Power Boost.
In Settings, Battery, set Power Saving Mode to Standard or Off.
Search Settings for Sleep mode and turn off Sleep mode optimization. It turns on airplane mode at night.

steps.title: Let Outage use the battery
steps: Open Settings, then Battery, then Battery Optimization.
Tap Outage and choose Don't optimize.
Open Settings, Apps, App Management, Outage, Battery. Turn on Allow Background Activity.

steps.title: Let Outage run in the background
steps: Open Settings, Apps, Special Access, Background Activity Permissions. Allow Outage.
If your phone has the Phone Master app, open Toolbox, then Auto-start management, and turn on Outage.

steps.title: Keep Outage in recent apps
steps: Open the recent apps screen.
Pin or lock the Outage card so it stays open.

steps.title: Turn off power savers that stop apps
steps: Open Settings, Battery, Power Saving Mode. Choose Standard or Off.
Open Settings, Special Features, XBoost. Turn off any mode that limits Outage.
In Game Mode settings, allow background data for Outage.

steps.title: If a name is missing
steps: Names change by version. Search Settings for battery, background and autostart.

Background activity is allowed for Outage
Auto-start is on for Outage, if your phone has it
Outage is pinned in recent apps

steps.title: Let Outage use the battery
steps: Open Settings, then Apps.
Tap the three dots at the top right, then Special app access.
Tap Battery optimization. Change the filter to All apps.
Tap Outage and choose Don't optimize.

steps.title: Let Outage start in the background
steps: Open the Phone Master app, then ToolBox, then Auto-start management.
Turn on Outage.

steps.title: Turn off power savers that stop apps
steps: Open Settings, then Battery.
Turn off any power saving mode.

steps.title: Keep Outage in recent apps
steps: Open the recent apps screen.
Pin or lock the Outage card so it stays open.

checklist.text: Battery optimization is off for Outage
Auto-start is on for Outage in Phone Master
Power saving modes are off
Outage is pinned in recent apps

steps.title: Let Outage use the battery
steps: Open Settings, Apps, Outage, Battery.
Choose Unrestricted.
If you see Battery optimization instead, choose All apps, tap Outage, and choose Don't optimize.

steps.title: Stop Samsung putting Outage to sleep
steps: Open Settings, Battery and device care, Battery, Background usage limits.
Turn off Put unused apps to sleep.
Remove Outage from Sleeping apps and Deep sleeping apps.
Add Outage to Never sleeping apps.
Search Settings for Adaptive battery and turn it off.

steps.title: Keep Outage in recent apps
steps: Open the recent apps screen.
Tap the Outage icon at the top of its card and choose Keep open.

steps.title: Check again after updates
steps: After a software update, open the same lists again. Samsung can put Outage back to sleep.

checklist.text: Battery is Unrestricted for Outage
Put unused apps to sleep is off
Outage is in Never sleeping apps
Adaptive battery is off
Outage is kept open in recent apps

steps.title: Let Outage start by itself
steps: Open the Security app, then Permissions, then Autostart.
Turn on Outage.
On newer versions you can also open Settings, Apps, Manage apps, Outage, App permissions, and allow Autostart.

steps.title: Remove battery limits
steps: Open Settings, Apps, Manage apps, Outage, Battery saver.
Choose No restrictions.
Or open the Security app, Battery, App battery saver, Outage, and choose No restriction.

steps.title: Keep Outage in recent apps
steps: Open the recent apps screen.
Drag the Outage card down, or press and hold it and tap the padlock.

steps.title: Turn off power savers
steps: Turn off Battery saver and Ultra battery saver.
If your phone has a Power plan setting, choose Performance.

checklist.text: Battery optimization is off for Outage
Autostart is on for Outage
Battery saver is set to No restrictions for Outage
Outage is locked in recent apps

steps.title: Let Outage use the battery
steps: Open Settings, Apps, Outage, Battery. On some versions it is called App battery usage.
Choose Unrestricted.
On older versions: open Advanced, Battery, Battery optimization, All apps, tap Outage and choose Not optimized.

steps.title: Check background limits
steps: In the same Battery screen, make sure Background restriction or Restricted is off for Outage.

checklist.text: Battery is Unrestricted for Outage
Background restriction is off for Outage

steps.title: Let Outage use the battery
steps: Open Settings and search for Battery optimization.
Find Outage and choose Don't optimize, Not optimized or Unrestricted.

steps.title: Let Outage run in the background
steps: Search Settings for Autostart, Auto-start or Background activity.
Allow Outage.

steps.title: Keep Outage in recent apps
steps: Open the recent apps screen.
Lock or pin the Outage card, if your phone offers it.

steps.title: Turn off power savers
steps: Turn off Battery saver and any power saving mode while Outage should watch.

Autostart or background activity is allowed for Outage, if your phone has it
